headline: Controlled tests show decision-model reliability depends on rule conflict, wording, and supplied information
summary: A 2026-10-21 arXiv paper proposes controlled tests of decision models using executable arithmetic rules, crossed rule/state cases, equivalent wording changes and manipulated value tables. The authors report that transfer gains depend on agreement with source examples; under fully conflicting rule quartets, results differ in sign across two source splits and joint correctness is low. In tests of TypeSafe's Jev service, answers change more across equivalent wordings than across identical-text repeats and often follow altered table values or mappings. These are author-reported results on synthetic finite-domain tasks and one service version; code and data are stated as forthcoming, and this activation did not independently reproduce the analyses.
